The problem reduces to avoiding a full “corner” \( \{a, a+e_1,\dots,a+e_r\} \) in the lattice of exponent vectors of the \(S\)-smooth numbers.  
An easy double‑counting argument shows that any set avoiding all such corners must miss at least a \(1/(r+1)\) fraction of the points, giving an upper bound of \(r/(r+1)\) for the density.  
Conversely, the coloring \( \phi(a)=\sum_{i=1}^r i a_i \pmod{r+1}\) partitions the lattice into \(r+1\) equally sized residue classes asymptotically; discarding the class \(\phi\equiv0\) yields a set of density \(r/(r+1)\) that contains no forbidden configuration. Hence the limit exists and equals \(r/(r+1)\).
